title: What Comes Next and Why: Interpretable Next-Event Prediction with Neuro-Symbolic Rules
claim: A two-phase training scheme learns interpretable symbolic rules first, then adds a residual network to boost accuracy while keeping rules frozen.
layout: 2 panels; (a) top-down two-column flow, (b) left-to-right layered network
description: Two panels. Panel (a), "Architecture of RUNES", is split by a dashed vertical line into a Symbolic Phase (rule learning) and a Predictive Phase (boosting accuracy). The same input box, a sequence and a time, feeds a blue RULES box on the left and a green Residual Network box on the right. Each box outputs a prediction: pink for the rules, green for the residual. A "frozen" arrow carries the rule output into a plus node. Cross-entropy loss boxes sit at the bottom. Panel (b), "Architecture of RULES", is a layered network read left to right. Input events (x, t) connect to blue event-time predicate neurons. These connect to orange conjunction (antecedent) neurons, which a plus node sums into a pink prediction. Dark and grey edges mark active versus inactive connections. Math notation labels each layer.
caption: \textit{Architecture overview of \ourMethodSideChannel{}.} (a) \ourMethodSideChannel{} is trained in two phases: \ourMethod{} first learns sequential rules, after which a residual network is trained with the \ourMethod{} network frozen. (b) \ourMethod{} represents rules in its layers: Neurons in the first layer encode event-time predicates. Neurons in the second layer select a subset of these predicates and combine them into conjunctions (antecedents). The output layer sums the softmax logits of all active rules to produce the final prediction.
abstract: In real-world applications, being able to explain why a prediction is made is often as important - if not more so - than achieving high accuracy. However, existing methods for sequential event prediction typically prioritize accuracy at the expense of interpretability. Neuro-symbolic approaches offer a promising direction to improve interpretability by learning symbolic rules, but extending them to next-event prediction is challenging due to the presence of temporal dependencies. We introduce RULES, a neuro-symbolic model that learns sequential rules directly from data, and combine it with a residual network to form RUNES (Rule Network for Event Sequences). RULES accurately recovers ground truth rules from synthetic data and discovers compact, interpretable rule sets on real data. RUNES combines these rules additively with a residual network, achieving competitive accuracy while providing transparent access to active rules and how residuals adjust predictions.
